attention_states.NEEDS_REVIEW: Harsh should inspect the decision and may KEEP, CHANGE, BLOCK, or DEFER_TO_OWNER.
attention_states.HUMAN_REQUIRED: The affected behavior is blocked on a genuinely human-reserved decision.
attention_states.FOR_AWARENESS: Material working decision for visibility. No response is required unless Harsh wants a change.
attention_states.OWNER_DEFERRED: Harsh has deferred the decision to the Carbon owner.
attention_states.RESOLVED: A durable response or superseding repository decision has resolved this attention item.

decisions.title: Generator package ownership
decisions.question: Should the bounded generator runtime live in the carbon.generators package with the Burgers fixture isolated beneath it?
decisions.recommendation: KEEP the current package ownership and one-way dependency boundary.
decisions.why: The package keeps generator authority distinct from Challenge authoring, reference truth, scoring, and later research-service ownership.
decisions.if_kept: B-03 remains a bounded generator seam that downstream B-04/B-05/B-06 work can consume without absorbing their authority.
decisions.if_changed: Package ownership, imports, code-authority rules, tests, and downstream references would need a prospective migration.

decisions.title: Exact request, event, and replay identity
decisions.question: Should generator request, event, result, and replay identities remain exact and immutable rather than ambient or mutable?
decisions.recommendation: KEEP exact immutable identity and replay bindings.
decisions.why: Generator evidence must be reproducible and auditable without allowing mutable aliases or hidden retries to reinterpret history.
decisions.if_kept: Downstream evidence can bind exact generation facts.
decisions.if_changed: Canonicalization, replay, persistence, and evidence lineage would need a versioned migration.

decisions.title: Role mapping and random-material boundary
decisions.question: Should B-03 consume A4-owned random material through closed role mappings instead of owning seed or entropy authority?
decisions.recommendation: KEEP A4 ownership of protected random material and closed B-03 role mappings.
decisions.why: Generation should consume authorized randomness without becoming the authority that creates or discloses protected seed material.
decisions.if_kept: Seeding and generation remain separate authority domains.
decisions.if_changed: A4 leakage boundaries, B-03 request semantics, and downstream replay assumptions would need review.

decisions.title: Six terminal generator outcomes
decisions.question: Should generation keep valid generation, registered exclusion, generator nonconformance, invalid construction, censored case, and infrastructure failure as distinct outcomes?
decisions.recommendation: KEEP the six-way typed outcome model.
decisions.why: Scientific failure, construction failure, censoring, exclusion, and infrastructure failure must not collapse into one candidate-failure bucket.
decisions.if_kept: B-04/B-05/B-06 can consume typed failure semantics without guessing cause.
decisions.if_changed: Failure ownership and evidence interpretation across downstream tickets would need a coordinated migration.

decisions.title: Visible attempt and successor accounting
decisions.question: Should every generation attempt remain visible with deferred successor finalization rather than silent retry or replacement?
decisions.recommendation: KEEP one visible derivation per attempt and explicit successor accounting.
decisions.why: The realized evidence population must not silently become easier than the intended sampled population.
decisions.if_kept: Later conformance and qualification work can audit intended-versus-realized evidence.
decisions.if_changed: Sampling, censoring, replacement, and qualification evidence semantics would need review.

decisions.title: Fact-only conformance and accounting
decisions.question: Should B-03 emit only factual support, censoring, accounting, and conformance evidence while leaving estimands and thresholds to later scientific authority?
decisions.recommendation: KEEP B-03 fact-only and leave scientific adequacy to B-05/B-06 and human-owned inputs.
decisions.why: The generator can report what happened without deciding whether the sampled population or evidence is scientifically adequate.
decisions.if_kept: Generator implementation stays mechanically useful without inventing scientific thresholds.
decisions.if_changed: Scientific authority would move into B-03 and conflict with later measurement/qualification ownership.

decisions.title: Fixed-viscosity structural Burgers fixture
decisions.question: Should Wave B use the fixed structural Burgers fixture only as a deterministic development fixture rather than a production scientific value?
decisions.recommendation: KEEP the fixed-viscosity Burgers realization structurally fixture-only.
decisions.why: Wave B needs executable structure while real population, range, viscosity, sampling, and qualification values remain human-owned and unavailable.
decisions.if_kept: B-03 can support authoring and conformance tests without claiming a qualified generator.
decisions.if_changed: Real scientific values would require explicit owner/science decisions and new evidence before use.

decisions.title: Fixture provenance, disclosure, and LIVE exclusion
decisions.question: Should fixture provenance be mandatory, public disclosure remain bounded, and every fixture-derived case remain structurally unable to satisfy LIVE qualification?
decisions.recommendation: KEEP explicit fixture provenance, safe disclosure, and structural LIVE exclusion.
decisions.why: A development fixture must never be confused with qualified scientific evidence or leak protected generation material.
decisions.if_kept: The fixture remains useful for engineering while fail-closing qualification and disclosure boundaries.
decisions.if_changed: A3 LIVE gating, public projection, security, and qualification logic would need coordinated review.

decisions.title: Canonical evaluation package and one-way ownership
decisions.question: Should B-04 keep and wrap the reserved carbon.evaluation namespace with one-way dependencies instead of creating a new reference owner or absorbing generator, scoring, registry, or qualification authority?
decisions.recommendation: KEEP + WRAP carbon.evaluation as B-04's package boundary and preserve one-way ownership.
decisions.why: The namespace is already the installed-wheel and code-authority seam for reference work, while a new package or placement under another domain would duplicate or collapse ownership.
decisions.if_kept: B-05, B-06, B-07F, and B-E2 can consume narrow named seams without granting B-04 their measurement, qualification, fixture-consumer, or expanded-runtime authority.
decisions.if_changed: Package ownership, imports, code-authority rules, exports, and downstream references would require a prospective migration before runtime types exist.

decisions.title: Canonical identity, refs, and prospective history
decisions.question: Should B-04 reserve a distinct v1 identity and ref inventory with strict canonicalization, immutable historical interpretation, and a separate exact-schema freeze before runtime?
decisions.recommendation: KEEP the distinct v1 identity/ref inventory, strict canonical requirements, prospective versioning, and required B-04-D11 freeze before runtime.
decisions.why: Reference policy, grants, runs, artifacts, comparisons, admission, and assets must bind every meaning-bearing identity without mutable aliases, ambient serialization, coercion, or latest-version lookup.
decisions.if_kept: B-05 and B-06 can consume stable refs, while B-E2 can test stale and cross-binding responses against immutable history.
decisions.if_changed: Canonical profiles, field registries, refs, consumers, and migration rules would change prospectively while historical bytes and their interpretation remain unchanged.

decisions.title: Separate evidence, authority, source, and composition axes
decisions.question: Should evidence kind, scientific authority function, source class, and target composition remain separate closed axes with exact policy containment and primary/witness disjointness?
decisions.recommendation: KEEP the orthogonal closed axes, exact membership rules, and separate SINGLE_ENTRY or REGISTERED_HYBRID_POLICY composition.
decisions.why: Analytic, numerical, experimental, industrial, surrogate, and hybrid labels describe evidence or source form rather than scientific authority and cannot safely substitute for registered primary or witness roles.
decisions.if_kept: B-05 can consume exact evidence meaning, B-06 can retain limitations, and B-E2/B-E3 can test and render role boundaries without source-count voting or self-promotion.
decisions.if_changed: Role, source, composition, policy, canonicalization, comparison, and downstream evidence contracts would need a prospective coordinated migration.

decisions.title: Policy-issued nominal primary and witness runner grants
decisions.question: Should nominal primary and witness requests, grants, runners, and outcomes remain separate, with trusted policy resolution binding an exact one-use grant before execution?
decisions.recommendation: KEEP separate nominal primary/witness paths, exact policy resolution, one-use grants, and no generic truth mode.
decisions.why: Caller-selected solvers, tolerances, payloads, paths, code, retries, or fixture flags would let execution choose or widen scientific authority.
decisions.if_kept: B-07F can consume minimal fixture assets and B-E2 can own Julia/service adapters and expanded runtime failures without making runners the policy authority.
decisions.if_changed: Runner families, policy resolution, grant identity, provider boundaries, failure outcomes, and downstream adapters would require new prospective types and policies.

decisions.title: Total run and comparison outcomes with failure attribution
decisions.question: Should reference runs and comparisons use closed total outcomes, subordinate reasons, deterministic precedence, and the unchanged B-02A reference-censoring eligibility map?
decisions.recommendation: KEEP total typed run/comparison outcomes, deterministic reason precedence, infrastructure-safe ambiguity, and exact B-02A censoring eligibility.
decisions.why: Missing, unresolved, contested, numerical, malformed, infrastructure, capacity, timeout, cancellation, and supported states must not collapse into candidate failure, score zero, or a partial answer.
decisions.if_kept: B-02A receives only eligible exact terminal facts, B-05 rejects unsupported material, and B-E2 can prove the complete runtime matrix.
decisions.if_changed: Every producer and consumer of terminal outcomes, comparison facts, censoring eligibility, and evidence admission would require an exhaustive prospective migration.

decisions.title: Positive-only TruthAsset admission and distinct fixture assets
decisions.question: Should a ReferenceArtifact become a TruthAsset only through a separate positive admission authority and exact eligible graph, while fixture output remains a distinct non-promotable asset?
decisions.recommendation: KEEP positive-only TruthAsset admission, separate grant issuance and substantive admission, exact rejection for absence or ineligibility, and structurally distinct FixtureReferenceAsset output.
decisions.why: Solver success, artifact presence, fixture provenance, booleans, wrappers, or self-admission cannot create answer-key authority or qualified evidence.
decisions.if_kept: B-05 consumes only admitted refs, B-06 owns qualification evidence, B-07F consumes fixture assets, and B-E2 cannot manufacture admission authority.
decisions.if_changed: Admission authority, capability issuance, artifact eligibility, qualification, fixture separation, disclosure, and downstream consumers would require a high-cost prospective science/security migration.

decisions.title: Explicit support, applicability, conditioning, and uncertainty
decisions.question: Should support, applicability, conditioning, and uncertainty remain case-level exact evidence bindings with no invented numeric floor, threshold, independence, or transfer assumption?
decisions.recommendation: KEEP explicit evidence-bound support, applicability, conditioning, uncertainty, dependence, limitations, and downstream-use restrictions without production numeric values.
decisions.why: Envelope labels, convergence, residuals, solver tolerances, mesh size, or witness differences do not by themselves establish applicability, conditioning, uncertainty, or independence.
decisions.if_kept: B-05 can own propagation and decision use, B-06 can qualify coverage and dependence, and B-E1 can test joint decision resolution while unsupported cases remain visible.
decisions.if_changed: Support policies, uncertainty identities, evidence applicability, measurement use, qualification, and historical evidence would require new versions and requalification.

decisions.title: Correlation disclosure, contested disagreement, and no fallback
decisions.question: Should material shared and distinct source paths be disclosed, disagreement remain contested or indeterminate, and fallback remain unavailable unless prospectively registered and qualified?
decisions.recommendation: KEEP explicit correlation disclosure, contested disagreement, no averaging, and no registered fallback.
decisions.why: Implementation labels, multi-code agreement, voting, averaging, assumed independence, or convenient fallback can hide common bias and silently change the answer-key contract.
decisions.if_kept: B-05/B-E1 can apply dependence-aware use, B-06 can retain evidence and limitations, and B-E2 can test disagreement and failure without converting them into candidate failure.
decisions.if_changed: Comparison, correlation, fallback, qualification, policy versioning, and historical evidence would require a prospective policy and requalification.

decisions.title: Complete provenance, cache identity, and protected disclosure
decisions.question: Should every meaning-bearing identity enter run and cache identity, every cache hit revalidate the full graph, and all raw reference material remain protected unless positively allow-listed?
decisions.recommendation: KEEP complete provenance and cache binding, full-graph hit validation, protected-by-default records, and positive allow-list public projection.
decisions.why: Partial keys, mutable tags, stale hits, paths, generic serialization, redaction after serialization, and diagnostics can substitute meaning or disclose protected answer-key material.
decisions.if_kept: B-06 can own retained qualification evidence, B-07F receives fixture-only projections, and later real cache and service owners can operate without widening disclosure.
decisions.if_changed: Cache identity, provenance, public projection, access, rights, security, operations, and every consumer would require explicit versioned review and migration.

decisions.title: Preserve B-02A censoring and downstream owner boundaries
decisions.question: Should B-04 supply exact reference facts through existing B-02A censoring semantics while leaving case lifecycle, measurement, qualification, fixture consumption, expanded adapters, and later authority with their named owners?
decisions.recommendation: KEEP the existing B-02A censoring model and one-way downstream owner boundaries; B-04 creates no second lifecycle, score, gate, Dossier, LIVE, product, frontier, or settlement path.
decisions.why: B-02A and B-03 already own canonical case and intended-versus-realized accounting, while B-05, B-06, B-07F, B-E1, B-E2, and B-E3 have explicit non-substitutable responsibilities.
decisions.if_kept: Reference and infrastructure failures remain distinct from candidate science, and each downstream ticket consumes only its authorized exact seam.
decisions.if_changed: Case lifecycle, censoring, measurement, qualification, fixture, adapter, LIVE, product, frontier, and economic owners would require a high-cost coordinated migration.

decisions.title: Repository-owned development throughput and delivery proof
decisions.question: Should Carbon make repository-owned canonical execution, path-aware CI, exact-head review, guarded merge policy, and external completion receipts the default delivery system before B-04 runtime resumes?
decisions.recommendation: KEEP the OWNER-DX-01 delivery system and its fail-closed exact-identity boundaries.
decisions.why: A single repository-owned path reduces workstation drift, avoidable reruns, generated-output fan-out, stale pull-request declarations, and unverifiable completion claims without transferring scientific or production authority to automation.
decisions.if_kept: B-01G and resumed B-04 work inherit one canonical validation path, a stable Merge gate, explicit review and merge evidence, and bounded Development Hub updates.
decisions.if_changed: Canonical execution, CI classification, branch protection, receipt authority, agent delivery protocol, and downstream ticket launch requirements would need a coordinated prospective migration.

decisions.title: Post-Wave-B Bittensor and treasury-before-mainnet roadmap
decisions.question: Should Carbon preserve Wave B, begin real Bittensor integration only afterward, prove temporary direct weights on testnet, and require frontier-backed treasury settlement before mainnet economic activation?
decisions.recommendation: KEEP OWNER-NET-01's C0/C1/C2, D-to-H-to-I, typed-intent, no-winner-sink, validator-evidence, and treasury-before-mainnet roadmap.
decisions.why: The roadmap proves network integration without letting Bittensor objects, raw score magnitude, stale winners, test fixtures, or direct mainnet winner weights acquire scientific or production economic authority.
decisions.if_kept: Wave B remains unchanged; G3 stays non-LIVE and non-settling; Wave D qualifies the first Challenge; Wave H alone creates frontier events; and Wave I must qualify treasury routing and settlement before mainnet activation.
decisions.if_changed: Launch taxonomy, network/science boundaries, typed intents, no-winner behavior, frontier sequencing, treasury custody and settlement, validator economics, migration evidence, and affected authority documents require a prospective owner-reviewed supersession.

decisions.title: Exact v1 executable reference schema and protected surface
decisions.question: Should B-04 freeze the exact closed v1 record/ref registry, subordinate schemas, outcome/reason and absence matrices, canonical framing, root exports, and protected types before its first runtime model?
decisions.recommendation: KEEP the recorded B-04-D11 v1 schema, compatibility matrices, one-to-one ref registry, audience-safe root tuple, and protected submodule boundary.
decisions.why: A complete pre-runtime freeze prevents role, identity, absence, provenance, artifact, admission, or public-surface ambiguity while preserving the ratified B-04-D1 through B-04-D10 meaning.
decisions.if_kept: B-04 can implement deterministic fixture-only policy, execution, comparison, artifact, admission, and disclosure paths while B-05, B-06, B-07F, and B-E2 consume only their authorized seams.
decisions.if_changed: Supersede B-04-D11 and prospectively update every affected schema field/type/order, ref mapping, compatibility test, protected/public boundary, and downstream consumer without reinterpreting merged v1 history.

decisions.title: At-most-once admission-authority invocation across the callback boundary
decisions.question: Should the one-use admission grant remain consumed after callback start even when the provider raises, is cancelled, or returns an invalid echo without producing a decision?
decisions.recommendation: KEEP complete pre-callback validation and reversible inspection, atomically consume immediately before the saved callback with no post-boundary rollback, and replace non-Exception provider control flow with one fixed protected signal outside provider context.
decisions.why: The ratified contract permits one exact attempt and selects no retry or durable idempotency policy; rollback could duplicate an unknowable external effect, while the original provider signal could disclose protected text, arguments, context, or traceback frames.
decisions.if_kept: Provider or post-callback failure creates no decision or TruthAsset, hostile control signals expose no provider payload and create no outcome, and every reentrant, concurrent, or later reuse fails locally before a second callback.
decisions.if_changed: A resumable design requires a prospective grant and service version, durable attempt identity, authority-side idempotency evidence, reconciliation states, and explicit operations and security ownership.

decisions.title: Manual Codex/GPT review plus distinct human approval
decisions.question: Should Carbon replace the inaccessible Greptile workspace with fresh complete-diff Codex/GPT review, a closed exact-head receipt, and distinct non-author human approval?
decisions.recommendation: KEEP GOV-REVIEW-01-D1 and its protected GPT review gate, stale-approval dismissal, last-push approval, resolved-thread, normal-merge, and no-bypass controls.
decisions.why: The owner-selected process preserves exact-head review and finding accountability without depending on an inaccessible third-party workspace or adding an automated model API secret and billing dependency.
decisions.if_kept: B-04 and later tickets receive one exact-head model-review record plus an attributable non-author human approval, while all scientific and other reserved authority stays separate and fail closed.
decisions.if_changed: Delivery protocol, receipt schema, review workflow and validator, ruleset artifact and live state, ticket gates, tests, and external completion evidence require a coordinated prospective migration.

decisions.title: Carbon Iterative Agent Harness Pilot
decisions.question: Should Carbon interpose a bounded identity-bound Planner/Developer/Tester controller after completed B-04 and before B-05 without changing B-05 science or final delivery authority?
decisions.recommendation: KEEP OWNER-DX-02 and B-01H-D1 through B-01H-D6: deterministic controller advancement, exact identities, manifest-authorized evidence independently replayed by the controller, regression-first replanning, sanitized role projections, audited progressive disclosure, and delivery-protocol-only final handoff.
decisions.why: PR #75 completed B-04 and selected B-05 but explicitly recorded B-05 as not started, allowing the development-system interposition without rewriting scientific requirements or historical evidence.
decisions.if_kept: B-01H can complete only in bounded development-tooling scope, after which B-05 becomes the active first pilot from the receipt-recorded exact main while all scientific and later authority remains human-owned and fail closed.
decisions.if_changed: Update OWNER-DX-02 and the B-01H ticket, plan, role boundaries, schemas, tests, Hub sequencing, and B-05 pilot mapping prospectively before relying on the affected controller behavior.
